summary: Verified and extended src/tests/workspace.manager.test.ts. The CRUD round-trip test (AC2) was missing — added it covering create→list→getById→update→rename→remove with full assertions. All other ACs were already covered by individual tests: invalid ID format rejection (4 variants), STABLE deletion prevention, STABLE rename prevention, duplicate ID rejection, DateModified updates on update() and rename(), and non-existent project error throwing. Full suite of 176 tests passes with no regressions.

comments.note: Added the missing CRUD round-trip test (create→list→getById→update→rename→remove). All other ACs were satisfied by focused individual tests already present. Full suite of 176 tests passes cleanly with no regressions.

summary: workspace.manager.test.ts passes code review. 40+ tests across 8 well-structured sections cover the full WorkspaceManager API: isStable, list (with WorkspaceInfo shape validation), getById, create (4 invalid-ID variants, non-existent project, duplicate, correct field defaults, persistence), update (field changes, DateModified, persistence), rename (STABLE protection, invalid newId, non-existent project/workspace, duplicate newId check, return values, DateModified, old-ID removal), remove (STABLE protection, not-found errors, deletion, isolation), and CRUD round-trip. All error regex patterns verified against implementation strings. makeProject() helper is a clean abstraction. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: makeProject() helper uses a fixed URL 'https://github.com/user/repo.git'. Since every test calls makeManagers(makeTempDir()) first, each RepositoryManager is fresh and the fixed URL never conflicts across tests. However, any future test calling makeProject() twice with the same repoManager would throw a duplicate-URL error. The helper has no guard against this. Low risk now, but worth a JSDoc note if the helper is extended.

[documentation-forward] The WP-008 spec description lists 'cross-project isolation' as a coverage target, but no test explicitly verifies that workspace operations on project A leave project B unaffected. Isolation is architecturally guaranteed (every method reads by projectId from a separate file), but a dedicated two-project isolation test would make the contract explicit and match the spec description. Consider adding as a follow-up test.
